DIV8.HEAD: § 9999.1 Authority and purpose.
DIV8.P: (a) Authority. This part is issued under the Example Act.
(b) Purpose. This part sets out the rights of consumers who use example transfers.

DIV8.HEAD: § 9999.2 Definitions.
DIV8.P: For the purposes of this part, the following definitions apply:
(a)(1) Access device means a card or code used to start a transfer.
(2) An access device becomes an accepted access device when the consumer uses it.
(b)(1) Account means a demand deposit account held by a consumer.
(i) It includes a savings account.
(ii) It does not include an account held under a bona fide trust agreement.
This paragraph has no marker and continues (b)(1)(ii).
(2) An account does not include an occasional or incidental credit balance.
(c) Business day means any day on which the offices of the institution are open.
(d) Consumer means a natural person.
(e) Credit means the right to defer payment of debt.
(f) Electronic terminal means an electronic device through which a consumer may start a transfer.
(g) Financial institution means a bank or any other person that holds an account.
(h)(1) Person means a natural person or an organization.
(i) Preauthorized transfer means a transfer authorized in advance to recur at substantially regular intervals.
(j) State means any State of the United States.

EXTRACT.P: (k) Unauthorized transfer means a transfer from an account started by a person other than the consumer without actual authority.

DIV8.HEAD: § 9999.3 Liability of consumer.
DIV8.P: (a) Conditions. A consumer may be liable for an unauthorized transfer only if the conditions in this section are met.
(b)(1) Timely notice. If the consumer notifies the institution within two business days, liability shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of transfers before notice.
(2) Late notice. If the consumer does not notify the institution within two business days, liability shall not exceed $500.
(i) The first limit applies to transfers before the close of the two business days.
(ii) The second limit applies to transfers after that.
(iii) A transfer on the day of notice counts as before notice.

DIV9.HEAD: Appendix A to Part 9999—Model Disclosure Clauses
DIV9.P: Tell us AT ONCE if you believe your card has been lost or stolen.
Our business days are Monday through Friday.

DIV9.HEAD: Supplement I to Part 9999—Official Interpretations
DIV9.P: 1. Examples. The term includes debit cards and personal identification numbers.
2. Checks. The term does not include a check.
1. Consumer asset account. The term includes a prepaid account.
